preview: Interview experience for a full-time role at Deutsche Bank, detailing the online assessment, multiple technical rounds, a pro-fit round, and an HR round.

Deutsche Bank FTE Interview Experience
Unnati Nandrekar B.Tech IT 2018-2022
Eligibility Criteria for the test:
70% or equivalent CGPA with no Standing Arrears
Branches: Computer Engineering, Information Technology and EXTC.
Online test:
The test was conducted on Hackerearth platform. There were three questions having 20, 50 and 50 marks.
1.
Given 2 arrays consisting of N integers representing the length of the sticks and the second array consisting of their frequencies respectively, the task is to find the maximum sum possible of all lengths of the squares and rectangles constructed using these sticks.
2.
Given a Binary string, the task is to find the largest Prime Number possible by the decimal representation of a subsequence of the given binary string. If no prime number can be obtained, print -1.
3.
Given an input string, the task is to find the smallest substring having “ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ” as a subsequence.
Round 1-Technical Round: 45 minutes
1.
Tell me about yourself.
2.
I had mentioned Java in my resume so he asked me why I chose Java and the differences between C++ and Java.
3.
Code Valid sudoku on Leetcode platform-https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-sudoku/
I could not solve it completely due to time constraints. The interviewer was patient and helped me to come up with the solution. He suggested his approach that he had used in python and asked me to do something similar in Java.
4.
Explain all the normal forms in Database-1NF, 2NF, 3NF
Then, he gave me a table and asked to identify which normal form the table belonged to.
I was able to identify it. It was in 1NF. He asked me how to break up the table to make it 2NF. I answered correctly and he was satisfied.
5.
Any questions?
Round 2-Technical Round: 45 minutes
1.
Tell me about yourself.
2.
Few questions about OOPS in Java.(Inheritance, polymorphism, difference between the two and other common questions).
3.
Code: An array contains n numbers which can be positive and negative numbers. Find the first missing positive number in the array. Here, you have to ask questions about n and the size of the array, whether the array is sorted or not and modify and optimize based on the constraints.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-the-smallest-positive-number-missing-from-an-unsorted-array/
4.
Code for Diagonal traversal of a Tree.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/diagonal-traversal-of-binary-tree/
5.
Puzzle: A man is at the bottom of a well that is 50m. Each day, the man climbs 4m up but comes back 3 m down. How many days does it take for him to come out of the well?
Answer: As the man climbs 1m effectively each day, on the 46th day he will be at 46m. Now he will climb 4m up i.e 46+4=50 and come out of the well. Thus the answer is 46 days.
6.
Code: Given a matrix(which is fixed with each test case) and a sequence of characters in the form of a string. You are standing at the top left corner of the matrix. Output a sequence consisting of ‘L’, ‘R’, ‘U’ and ‘D’ for left, right, up and down respectively. This output sequence shows the path of minimum length to cover the input string while travelling across the matrix.
Matrix: a b c d e
e f g h i
j k l m n
String: aej
Output: DD
Round 3: Pro-fit round: 30 minutes
1.
Tell me about yourself.
2.
Few questions about OOPS in Java.(Inheritance, polymorphism, difference between the two, difference between interfaces and abstract classes, other common questions).
They always try to confuse you, be confident and answer to the best of your knowledge.
If you don’t know something, say no.
3.
Asked about my internship experience and some follow up questions.
4.
When will you use Merge sort and Quicksort?
5.
Asked me if I had used Javascript before, I said no. He asked what other technologies are you familiar with. I said Django but he wasn't familiar with it. He asked me how I kept myself updated with the current market requirements. I clarified and spoke about my interests and he was satisfied.
6.
Why do you want to work in Deutsche Bank?
7.
Why should we hire you?
8.
Any questions?
Round 4: HR - 15 minutes
1.
Tell me about yourself.
2.
How is college conducting your classes? Are you comfortable with online classes? What is the major difference between online and offline classes? What challenges did you face due to online classes and how did you tackle them?
3.
What according to you is your biggest achievement?
4.
What challenges did you face during COVID-19 pandemic and how did you tackle them?
5.
What has this pandemic taught you?
6.
Any questions?
Tips:
1.
Read GFG archives. They give you an idea about the type of questions asked and prepare accordingly.
2.
DSA is important, but so is theory. Do not ignore it.
3.
For coding problems, start with brute force and work your way up to the optimized solutions. Before starting, always ask questions about the problem instead of assuming things.
4.
Practice DSA problems with time and space complexities.
5.
Always ask questions at the end of the interview, it shows that you are interested.
6.
Pay attention to the pre-placement talk carefully. They often ask questions based on this talk. For round 3 and 4, go through the company website and try to remember the company values and incorporate these values in your answers.
7.
Always be confident irrespective of your preparation status.
